qns_content.text: A gas occupies a volume of 11.2 litres at STP. How many molecules are present in this gas? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\))

text_solutions:
Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres/mol.

Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \( \frac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5 \, \text{mol} \).

Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 0.5 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 3.01 \times 10^{23} \).

qns_content.text: The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) at 1 atm. What will it be at 0.25 atm if temperature remains constant?

text_solutions:
\(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto P\). If \(P\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(n\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(l\) increases 4 times.

New \(l = 8 \times 10^{-7} \times 4 = 3.2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}\).

qns_content.text: The ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\)) for a triatomic gas with no vibrational modes is:

text_solutions:
Triatomic gas: 3 translational + 3 rotational = 6 degrees of freedom.

\(C_v = 3R\), \(C_p = C_v + R = 4R\).

\(\gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{4R}{3R} = \frac{4}{3} = 1.33\).

qns_content.text: The mean free path of air molecules at STP is \(2.9 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\). If temperature doubles at constant pressure, what is the new mean free path?

text_solutions:
\(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), \(n = \frac{N}{V}\), and \(PV = Nk_B T\).

At constant \(P\), \(V \propto T\), so \(n \propto \frac{1}{T}\). If \(T\) doubles, \(n\) halves, \(l\) doubles.

New \(l = 2 \times 2.9 \times 10^{-7} = 5.8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).
